title_yt: A Stranger Offers You This Coin Flip... Do You? #Shorts
title_fb: May stranger na nag-alok ng coin flip... G ka ba?
hook: What if a hooded stranger says: heads, you win $150?
open_loop: Line 4 ('Weird part? This flip is on your side.') plants two questions: why is a bad-looking deal actually good, and why did a stranger offer it at all? The brain half (loss aversion, about 2x) lands in lines 5-6; the stranger half ('he bet you'd run') pays off in line 9, inside the last ~5 s before the A/B ending.
payoff: Your brain weighs a loss about twice as heavily as a win, so the $100 loss feels like about $195 and you run. But each flip pays you +$25 on average, and over 100 flips the chance you end up losing is under 2%. Twist: the stranger is the one taking the bad side; he offers it because he is betting you'll run, like most people do.

lines.text: Weird part? This flip is on *your* side.

List of two rows pops on the words: 'A  FLIP' (mark check) on 'flip', 'B  RUN' (mark x) on 'run'. Small badge 'Not financial advice' in the corner the whole scene. Hard cut on 'You?' disclaimer_on_screen: Not financial advice (corner badge, final scene; a brain/decision thought experiment, not advice to gamble). Spoken caveat: 'One flip's still 50/50.'

facts_used.claim: In the coin toss (win $150 / lose $100), most people decline ('You run' / 'He bet you'd run').
Most people reject the 50/50 win $150 / lose $100 flip even though it is positive on average (corroborating).
Losses are treated as about twice as large as an equivalent gain; named loss aversion.
Meta-analysis mean loss-aversion coefficient 1.955 (about 2x), so a $100 loss feels like about $195.
The ratio varies by context (hence 'about twice', 'about $195').
+$25 average per flip; over 100 fair flips the chance of a net loss is 1.76% (<2%); a single flip is 50/50.

changes_from_previous: Owner: 'walang what if' -> the first spoken words are now 'What if a hooded stranger says: heads, you win one fifty?' (v3 opened 'Heads, you win...').

Owner: 'hindi hookable' -> the hook is now a picturable situation with a character and tension at 0 s (a glowing-eyed stranger offers Benny a coin), not a bare math question. Stakes ('Tails, you lose $100') land by ~3 s.

Owner: 'hindi nakaka-entertain' -> rewritten as a mini cartoon: Benny wants the $150, gets scared, runs away, gets bonked by a coin, comes back smug and makes the stranger sweat. Visual gags every 2-4 s (NOPE stamp + sprint, peek-back, brain shaking, coin bonk + tear, jaw drop, stranger's grin flipping to panic).

Twist added: the stranger is the one on the losing side (-$25 a flip); he offers it because he bets you'll run, like most people. This is the 'wait, what?' moment and pays off the line-4 open loop in the last ~5 s.
Lecture removed: no pie chart or split-screen calculator; bars and counters appear only as quick props inside the story beats. '150 studies' and '+$2,500' dropped to keep one clean idea per beat.
Length: 89 spoken words (v3: 112) = ~34.2 s at 2.6 wps, inside the 25-35 s gate; 10 lines/scenes.

Ending: A/B comment choice ('A: flip. B: run. You?') with a hard cut that loops to the stranger's offer. Hedges kept: 'about twice', 'about $195', 'One flip's still 50/50', 'Not financial advice' on screen.
